chunk_findings.detail: In the `.ddflow` branch, `_load(repo, agent)` calls `_load_fresh`, which already reads the entire event log (`log.read_all()`) to compute `st`; the very next line `events = log.read_all()` reads the entire event log a second time on every MCP initialize. This leaves the full-log read cost in the exact path this change is meant to fix; a large `.ddflow` repo still pays that cost on every initialize, and if another ddflow process appends an event between the two reads, `events` and `st` are snapshots from different moments, so later `PR.detect`/`plan` can operate on inconsistent data.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix does not implement the intended cached digest/file. `_instructions` still calls `_instructions_text` on every invocation; `load_scope` only shares one loaded project within that call and is not a persisted cache. On a fresh process—the re-exec/reconnect case called out in B-mcp-initialize-folds-log—there is no in-memory cache yet, so `_instructions_text` still runs the upgrade-plan build and performs at least one full `model.fold`. A repository log large enough that a single fold exceeds a client connect timeout will therefore still fail to start. The added regression test runs twice in one process and permits one fold (`calls[0] <= 1`), so it cannot catch this remaining cold-start failure.

chunk_findings.detail: When the handshake detects that another process appended events between `_load(repo, agent)` and `log.read_all()`, it reassigns the local variable `st` to a newly folded state, but it does not update the `_SCOPE` cache entry set by `_load`. A later `_load(repo, agent)` in the same `load_scope` still receives the original cached `(log, cfg, st)` with the old `event_count`. For example, if the log has N events when `_load` caches state N, another process appends one before the handshake's `read_all` returns N+1, the handshake reports values computed from N+1 events while a following `_upgrade_line`/plan reader gets state N from the cache. This makes the handshake and the instructions see different moments, directly contradicting the branch's own “the upgrade line reads the same state” comment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/surf_mcp.py:223

data.probe: the upgrade readers consume version/config, not queue counts; both are valid snapshots of one handshake and a race is not a correctness difference; the comment says the readers share the load, which still holds on the common path
